_README: CI JOB BUDGET — the DEPLOYMENT DECLARATION.
Read by `.claude/bin/ci-job-budget-audit.mjs`, which is the generic ENGINE and
carries ZERO values from any deployment: no runner label, no capacity number, no
host identifier, no workflow filename. Every such value is read from THIS file.
That split is the whole point — the engine cascades to every USE template and
BUILD repo through the normal artifact flow, and this file never does.
COPY INSTRUCTION
cp .claude/bin/ci-job-budget.local.example.json \
.claude/bin/ci-job-budget.local.json
$EDITOR .claude/bin/ci-job-budget.local.json
NEVER CASCADES. `.claude/bin/*.local.json` matches `LOOM_LOCAL_PATTERNS` in
`.claude/bin/sync-tier-aware.mjs`, so the real file is skipped on EVERY sync lane
(reason `loom_local`) — USE and BUILD alike. Only THIS `.example` is committed and
distributed. `*.local.example.json` does not match `*.local.json`, which is why the
example travels and the declaration does not. Do NOT put a real runner label, org
slug, hostname, or internal workflow name in this committed template — every token
below is synthetic.
OVERRIDE
$CI_JOB_BUDGET_DECLARATION (an ABSOLUTE path) takes precedence over the local
file. Precedence: $CI_JOB_BUDGET_DECLARATION > ci-job-budget.local.json >
fail-LOUD. There is no default declaration and no positional fallback: an audit
with no declaration reports UNKNOWN and exits non-zero, never green.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A per-PR job fan-out is bounded by real runner capacity. Left
undeclared it grows until one pull request cannot validate without saturating the
fleet, and two concurrent pull requests become structurally impossible. Every job
reachable from a `pull_request` trigger must be one of:
required  — it provides a branch-protection required context (it IS the gate)
gated     — a per-JOB relevance skip, or a paths:-filtered workflow providing
no required context
budgeted  — listed under `budgeted` below, with a rationale a reviewer approved
Anything else is UNBUDGETED and the audit fails.
NOT A paths: FILTER. A required context inside a paths:-filtered workflow NEVER
REPORTS, and wedges the pull request at 'Expected — Waiting for status to be
reported'. The sanctioned shape for a required context is an unconditional trigger
with a per-JOB skip.
_fleets_why: A FLEET is a set of physical runners with one measured total. Pools draw from a
fleet; a pool's capacity can never exceed its fleet's, and the non-overlay pools
of one fleet can never SUM past it.
FRESHNESS IS FAIL-CLOSED, and this is the contract's load-bearing half. Every
capacity-bearing node — each fleet and each pool — MUST carry all three of:
capacity                 a finite positive number
capacity_authority       >= 40 chars naming HOW the number was obtained, and
RESTATING it as the literal `capacity <n>`
capacity_verified_as_of  a real ISO date, not in the future
A missing, unreal, or future date is a finding. A read older than
`capacity_max_age_days` (clamped by the engine, see below) is a finding. The audit
REFUSES rather than trusting a stale ceiling — a declared number whose freshness
nothing evaluates is a policy constant wearing a measurement's clothes.
WHY THE AUTHORITY STRING AND NOT JUST A DATE. A date alone reads identically
whether the number was re-measured or merely re-typed, so it cannot discriminate
between fresh and restated. The authority names the command or procedure a reader
can RE-RUN, and the `capacity <n>` restatement makes the sentence answerable to the
number: move the capacity without re-deriving the sentence and the audit reds.
NO CREDENTIAL IS REQUIRED FOR CORRECTNESS. `--verify-capacity` is an OPTIONAL
reconciliation for an operator who holds an API credential; it compares the
declared numbers against a live reading. Correctness does NOT depend on it, and it
is not the freshness gate. An engine whose only capacity reader needs a credential
no CI secret carries has no reader at all.

self-hosted.capacity_authority: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. Replace with your own: name the exact command a reader can re-run and restate the number it returned, e.g. `<runner-api-list-command>` returning capacity 12 registered and online.
self-hosted._oversubscribe_why: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE RATCHET, not an allowance. floor(12 x 2) = 24 = exactly today's fleet-wide worst-case demand, so any job added anywhere fails this audit in the diff that adds it. Replace with your own derivation. REVIEW BY 2026-11-16: if this value has not fallen, that is the finding.

vendor-hosted.capacity_authority: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE for a fleet that is NOT in the self-hosted runner API — a vendor-hosted pool whose ceiling is set by billing or runner-group configuration. Name that surface and restate what it showed: capacity 2 concurrent.

_pools_why: A POOL is a set of runner LABELS with a shared capacity. A job's `runs-on` is
tokenised and matched against these labels; a label declared by two pools is
ambiguous and resolves to NOTHING rather than being arbitrated.
`union: true` marks an OVERLAY pool whose runners are already counted in a sibling
pool of the same fleet. It excludes the pool from the capacity SUM and from
nothing else: it does NOT exempt the pool from its own ceiling, from the fleet
bound, or from the freshness contract. A `union: true` with no dated `_union_why`
is a finding — one key must never buy an exemption silently.
`oversubscribe` is the declared allowance. 1.0 means one pull request must fit the
pool outright. Above 1.0 it MUST carry `_oversubscribe_why` with a >= 40-char
rationale, an unexpired `REVIEW BY <YYYY-MM-DD>`, and the literal arithmetic
`floor(<capacity> x <ratio>) = <ceiling>` so the sentence notices either operand
moving. It is also PINNED: the ceiling must EQUAL today's worst case, never stand
above it, or the slack is free job slots nothing reds on.

pool-alpha.capacity_authority: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. Name the command that enumerated this label and restate what it returned: capacity 8 runners carrying example-label-alpha.
pool-alpha._oversubscribe_why: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE RATCHET. floor(8 x 2) = 16 = exactly today's worst case on this pool, so any added job reds in its own diff. Replace with your own derivation and re-derive whenever the CENSUS changes, not only when jobs are added. REVIEW BY 2026-11-16: if this has not fallen, that is the finding.

pool-beta.capacity_authority: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. Name the command that enumerated this label and restate what it returned: capacity 4 runners carrying example-label-beta.

pool-union._union_why: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE OVERLAY. This label is carried by every runner in the fleet, so its runners are already counted in pool-alpha and pool-beta and it must not be SUMMED with them. It is still held to its own ceiling and to the fleet bound. REVIEW BY 2026-11-16: confirm the label is still fleet-wide.
pool-union.capacity_authority: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. Name the command showing this label spans the whole fleet and restate the number: capacity 12 runners carry example-label-any.

pool-vendor.capacity_authority: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE for a vendor-hosted pool. Name the billing or runner-group surface that sets the concurrency and restate it: capacity 2 concurrent.

_required_contexts_why: The branch-protection required contexts, by CHECK-RUN NAME — the string GitHub
reports, which is a job's `name:` when it has one and its job ID when it does not.
ANTI-VACUITY: an EMPTY set is a finding, not a clean pass. With no required
contexts every job reads as non-required, so every job in a paths:-filtered
workflow reads as gated and the whole contract becomes undetectable.
A job whose `name:` interpolates a template can NEVER string-equal a required
context, because the check-run is reported under the unexpanded template. Such a
job must be declared under `_template_named_jobs` below or given a literal name.
_budgeted_why: An entry here is an EXEMPTION: a job that runs per-PR, gates nothing, and is
nevertheless kept. Each MUST carry a rationale that survives a reviewer asking
'why is this worth a runner slot on every pull request?'.
An exemption with no rationale is a permanent excuse — a deferral whose wake-up
condition nothing evaluates. The audit therefore fails a `why` shorter than 40
characters, one with no `REVIEW BY <YYYY-MM-DD>`, one whose date has passed, and
one whose date is further out than the review horizon.
EMPTY ON PURPOSE at introduction. Populating it is a REVIEWED act: the first audit
run enumerates the current unbudgeted jobs, and each one is then gated, promoted to
required, moved off the pull-request trigger, or declared here with a reason.
Pre-seeding it from the failing run launders today's drift into tomorrow's
baseline, which is the ratchet this file exists to stop.
_template_named_jobs_why: Jobs whose `name:` contains a template interpolation. Such a job's check-run is
reported under the UNEXPANDED template string, so the name can never string-equal a
branch-protection required context; promoting one to required would wedge every
pull request at 'Expected — Waiting for status to be reported'.
Declared rather than failed, because a template-named job that is NOT required is
LATENT rather than a live defect. An UNDECLARED one is a finding; so is a STALE
entry here, because leaving one standing pre-approves the next. Each entry needs
the same dated rationale every sibling exemption on this surface carries.
_capacity_max_age_days_why: How old the read behind a declared capacity may be before the audit REFUSES.
CLAMPED BY THE ENGINE. The effective window is min(this value, the engine's hard
ceiling), so a deployment may TIGHTEN it and can never loosen it. Without the clamp
this key would be a one-token way to make a stale ceiling fresh — raising the
window is the same move as raising the number it protects.
